# ADR-001 — Country routing and published content

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-01-architecture-approval.md))  
**Applies to** US-01, with shared boundaries for US-02 and US-03  
**Basis** [US-01 Draft 3](../../spec/US-01.md), [specification approval](../approvals/US-01-spec-approval.md), assessment pp. 1–3 and 6–9

## Context

One Angular build serves Colombia and Chile. Editors publish independent country configuration in Strapi. The URL identifies the active country, including on reload and browser Back or Forward. The frontend needs published content and all customer and quote data stays in the browser.

## Proposed decision

- Use one client-rendered Angular application and one standalone Router tree. Serve the country selector at `/` and recognize `/:country/quote/details` for US-01. Reserve `plans` and `summary` children for the later steps. An explicit in-country entry route may link to Details. Unsupported country segments show the recoverable country-selection screen and retain the attempted URL. Accept exact uppercase `CO` and `CL` and replace the history entry with the lowercase canonical path for the same country. Other case variants remain unsupported. SPA navigation fallback applies to app paths, with API paths and asset requests kept separate.
- Decode the current Router parameter to `co | cl` before accessing content or quote state. React to parameter changes even when the Router reuses the component. Same-country wizard navigation can reuse its last valid, in-memory configuration. Initial load, page reload, country transition (including return to a previously visited country), and explicit retry require a new request. Clear ready status at refresh start. Cancel superseded reads and check both country and request generation before committing a response. A late or failed response leaves quote data intact and never renders as current. The URL carries the country and step only.
- Use a Strapi country enum, Draft & Publish, and one **Form Configuration collection document per country**, containing the complete field list as repeatable components. Each field inherits country from its owning form. This makes punctuation, copy, additions and removals, ordering, and option or validation edits one publishable snapshot. Editors use Content Manager for entries and may stage drafts without changing the live form. The serving controller reads published documents explicitly and treats multiple published form documents for one country as invalid rather than picking a winner. Seed by country without clobbering subsequent editorial changes. A stable editorial field key is distinct from Strapi's internal component IDs. [Strapi Document Service publication status](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/status)
- US-02 can use a separate Plan collection filtered by requested country, published status, and active flag, with stable plan identifiers, ordered plans, stored price/currency, coverages, benefits, and a recommended flag. US-03 can use a separate country Terms document with published text and a revision identifier. Their precise shapes, prices, and publication/acceptance rules belong to their future specifications. Changes to plans or terms need only their own publication.

## Public read boundary

The browser uses a same-origin `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/form` routed to Strapi through the static app host. Keep Strapi's ordinary Content API authorization enabled and grant the Public role the single custom `api::quote-content.quote-content.readForm` action. Enable neither generated CRUD routes for these content types nor public draft, preview, plugin, search, media, or admin actions. The frontend sends no authorization token. The static host proxies the dedicated read path only and returns no substitute SPA HTML for unmatched API paths. Admin access is a separate local binding and uses Strapi admin authentication for editorial access. [Strapi routing](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/backend-customization/routes), [Users & Permissions](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/features/users-permissions)

The controller takes the canonical country path parameter and no caller-controlled filters, locale, population, or publication selectors. It explicitly queries published data, populates only the known components, validates the whole content projection, and maps an allowlisted DTO. Success is `200` with `{ schemaVersion: 1, country, fields }` (see [ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md)). Public outcomes are `400 INVALID_REQUEST` for unsupported query inputs, `404 UNSUPPORTED_COUNTRY` for an unsupported API path code, `404 FORM_NOT_PUBLISHED` for no published document, `503 FORM_UNAVAILABLE` for configuration invalidity or duplicate documents, and `503 CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE` for CMS retrieval failure. A published document with no fields is invalid. Use a stable `{ error: { code } }` response without stack traces, internal IDs, or raw data. Use `Cache-Control: no-store` on these responses and bypass intermediary cache for this API path. The frontend still decodes success bodies and rejects country or version mismatches. Errors use local accessible fallback copy and retry. Future plan and terms routes require separate public actions after those stories' approvals.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| URL query, cookies, or geolocation | A query is shareable but easier to drop between steps. Device-derived defaults conflict with explicit URL country selection. |
| One frontend per market or per-locale builds | Independent releases could isolate releases, at the cost of duplicate deployment and violating the single-build requirement. |
| Strapi i18n as the country axis | Convenient for translations of shared records. Country controls eligibility, currency, and fields as well as language, so a country enum models the business boundary directly. |
| One Strapi record per field with public collection reads | Easier independent field editing, with more fragmented publication, larger permission surface, and more coupling to Strapi's REST shape. |
| An authenticated BFF with a server-side Strapi token | Supports private content at the cost of additional runtime and secret management. The proposed custom Strapi route already serves a narrow public projection. |

The custom route and decoder are deliberate maintenance costs. Editors can publish changes within the supported versioned vocabulary. New field primitives and incompatible contract changes are engineering changes. Confirm exact Public action registration and route permissions in the pinned Strapi version during implementation before exposing the route. Verify both canonical URLs after a hard reload, draft exclusion, rejection of cross-country responses and query overrides, denial of anonymous writes and generated reads, and published change pickup without rebuilding Angular. Trace to AC-US01-01, 05, 08, 09, 11 and 13 and T-US01-01, 06, 08, 09, 11 and 13.

[Angular route state](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/read-route-state), [Angular deep-link deployment](https://angular.dev/tools/cli/deployment)
# ADR-002 — Typed dynamic form contract and reconciliation

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-01-architecture-approval.md))  
**Applies to** US-01, with stable fields and roles for US-02 and US-03  
**Basis** [US-01 Draft 3](../../spec/US-01.md), especially AC-US01-02–04, 07–10 and 12–16, and [ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md)

## Context

Strapi editors need to change field content and validation without rebuilding Angular. The application must reject a bad configuration atomically, preserve a compatible draft across changes, and display one configured error per field. A dynamic CMS key cannot provide static knowledge of its eventual widget or value type.

## Proposed decision

### Contract and failure behavior

Decode `unknown` once at each trust boundary using framework-independent TypeScript guards that produce a discriminated `FieldDefinition` union. A small shared workspace contract can supply the decoder, pure validation and fixtures to Strapi's projection and Angular's consumer. It carries no Angular or Strapi dependency and no customer data. Keep Strapi's nested editor representation behind its explicit projection. Contract version 1 is a fixed envelope with an exact version, the requested canonical country, and a nonempty fields array. Render content strings as text, including labels, help and errors. Each field has the following projected properties.

| Property | Version 1 proposal |
| --- | --- |
| `id`, `label`, `helpText`, `errorMessage` | Stable editor-maintained ID unique within the country form, Spanish label and fallback field error, and a required help-text property that permits an empty string. IDs are restricted opaque strings, protected from reserved object keys and independent of labels, order, and Strapi component IDs. |
| `kind`, `required`, `order` | One supported kind, a Boolean required flag, and a nonnegative safe-integer order. Sort by order, then by ID on a tie. Country is inherited from the form. |
| `rules` | Ordered array, possibly empty. Each rule specifies a recognized operator, its typed arguments when relevant, and its configured Spanish message. Order is the editor's array order. |
| `options`, `defaultValue` | Options are permitted only on selects and require stable unique option IDs and nonempty labels within each select. An omitted default means unset. A present default must meet the field's representation, available options, and configured rules. Fresh required selects start unset, so publishing a default for one is invalid. |
| `purpose` | Optional semantic marker, unique per reserved role. A usable form contains one required `dateOfBirth` date with `minimumAge` 18 and one required `vehicleYear` number with `vehicleYearRange`. `identityDocument` and `licensePlate` markers, when present, use text fields. This enables masking and pricing without relying on visible labels. |

Reject missing mandatory properties, missing published fields, date or number representation errors in rule arguments, incompatible defaults, unknown types or operators, duplicate IDs, and required selects with no valid options. Validate each option. An invalid option definition fails the snapshot. Allow an optional select to have no options and remain unset. Reject inverted range endpoints and a duplicate required rule. A rejected refresh never partially updates the view or the stored draft. Apply the error and retry behavior in ADR-001. Enforce size limits on fields, options, and text at the contract boundary. Choose exact limits during implementation against fixtures and document them.

### Type and rule compatibility

| Kinds and values | Supported operators |
| --- | --- |
| Text, a string, including document numbers and plates | `required`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `email` |
| Number, a finite JavaScript number | `required`, `min`, `max`, `vehicleYearRange` for the vehicle-year purpose |
| Select, a listed stable option ID string | `required` |
| Date, a valid Gregorian ISO calendar-date string `YYYY-MM-DD` | `required`, `minDate`, `maxDate`, `minimumAge` for the date-of-birth purpose |
| Checkbox, a Boolean | `required`, which requires explicit `true` for a required checkbox |

- Keep a single required check. The field flag controls requiredness. An optional explicit `required` rule is valid only when the flag is true and supplies the required message. A required flag without the rule uses the field's configured error message. Required checks distinguish missing values from numeric zero. Whitespace-only text is empty for the required check and stored document or plate strings retain leading zeros. Non-required rules treat an unset value as inapplicable. An invalid typed entry is distinct from an unset value. Apply validators to every field and retain the ordered outcomes. The required error wins when present, then the first failing configured rule, then the field fallback for an invalid representation no configured rule describes.
- Length and age arguments are nonnegative integers, and lengths count Unicode code points. Numeric bounds are finite and inclusive. Vehicle year requires a safe integer and uses local browser Gregorian year Y with inclusive Y−20 through Y+1. Date bounds are valid ISO dates and inclusive. Calculate age using Gregorian calendar components and the browser's local civil date via an injectable clock, avoiding UTC parsing shifts. Propose March 1 for a February 29 birthday in non-leap years in the simulator. `required`, `email`, and `vehicleYearRange` take no argument.
- Treat patterns as declarative whole-value checks in a bounded safe subset. Propose bounded character classes, literal segments, and bounded repetitions, with no backreferences, lookaround, groups, or unbounded repetition. Cap both pattern and input lengths. Use a bounded non-backtracking matcher for the subset or equivalent implementation whose cost is bounded on rejected input. Validate editor patterns before the config reaches ready state. This makes formatting changes publishable while keeping pattern matching predictable.

### Angular form and accessibility

Use Typed Reactive Forms with `FormRecord<FormControl<FieldValue | null>>` and a discriminated field/view model. Keys are dynamic and the control's static value type is the common union. Narrow by the decoded field kind and normalize at the control adapter and output boundaries. Use actual typed number and Boolean values, preserve meaningful empty or unset state, and track rendered elements by stable ID. Stay with native inputs and selects and an unset, non-selectable required-select placeholder. The first invalid field gets focus on an unsuccessful Continue. Keep Continue available after the configuration is ready, with application validation controlling progress and custom messages. Use native form semantics with an explicit Angular submit handler and no browser validation bubbles masking configured messages. On blur expose that field's message, on change reevaluate touched fields, and on submit expose all applicable errors. Associate visible errors and help through stable DOM IDs and `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid` when showing an error. Use concise status announcements for loading and retry, and avoid announcing the same validation error twice when moving focus. [Angular typed forms](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/typed-forms)

### Deterministic reconciliation

Rebuild the draft from the latest valid fields by ID instead of mutating the old key map in place. Omit removed or replaced IDs and obsolete select options entirely. For new IDs apply a valid allowed default or leave unset. For existing IDs preserve representable values and keep label, help, and order edits independent, even if updated business rules make a preserved value invalid. This lets users correct a value after a stricter constraint is published. Check the previous kind as well as the primitive value. Preserve a date as text, or text as a date only when it is already a valid ISO date. Clear other kind changes without implicit coercion. Select values require membership in the new option IDs and never migrate by label. Revalidate every field against the current clock and refreshed rules, write the clean snapshot atomically, and gate progression on the result. A restored valid required select stays selected. A fresh one, or one with an obsolete selection, shows its placeholder.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Hardcoded Angular fields or a FormGroup with fixed keys | Strong static key typing, with a code change for each CMS field change. |
| Untyped forms or a general JSON Schema rendering engine | Simpler generalization, with weaker app-level typing or an extra dependency and a harder-to-explain CMS contract. |
| Signal Forms | Fits a signal-first model and is stable in Angular 22. The proposed Angular 21 baseline and requested form preference favor Typed Reactive Forms. Signals still own non-control state. |
| Directly execute CMS regexes or arbitrary editor rules | Broader flexibility, with less predictable runtime cost and harder validation of whole snapshots. |

The proposal makes unsupported widgets and rule language changes schema work. It protects the required age and year invariants while permitting published changes to supported field content. The type matrix, safe pattern subset, date boundary convention, and required-select default restriction are proposed architecture decisions. Verify DTO acceptance and rejection in both consumers, age and year boundaries, required-first and rule order, data reconciliation, stale response rejection, keyboard focus, and the two required-select states. See T-US01-02–06, 08–10, 12 and 14–16. The final quote-summary view remains under US-03.
# ADR-003 — Frontend-only wizard state

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-01-architecture-approval.md))  
**Applies to** US-01, with shared state boundaries for US-02 and US-03  
**Basis** [US-01 Draft 3](../../spec/US-01.md), assessment pp. 2 and 6–9, and project owner's frontend-only data boundary

## Context

Step 1 must restore a draft when navigating back and reconcile from a newly retrieved form. Later steps depend on the same vehicle and policyholder data, plan selection, and terms and simulated payment status. Strapi owns business content. It does not receive customer, vehicle, quote, plan selection, or payment data.

## Proposed decision

Use a small Angular Signals store with explicit commands, typed snapshots, and read-only projections. Scope it to the app's quoting flow so route components can be recreated. Pass the country's decoded Router value to state accessors and store separate country snapshots. Never read a previous country's data while a new country is loading. Store normalized typed drafts with original field kind and stable field identifier; keep touch/submit and focus state in the component. The reconciler atomically replaces the active snapshot after a valid refresh and the store supplies the later-step projection only for the active country.

Use a small versioned, tab-scoped `sessionStorage` envelope for fictitious wizard state. The signal store owns the current state; the adapter writes full snapshots and validates the restored shape and country. Treat browser storage as untrusted, revalidate fields against freshly retrieved content before advancing, and reject malformed or unknown-version stored data. A recoverable content error retains the draft but blocks progression. If storage is blocked or fails, continue using memory for the current page session and make reload recovery unavailable. Clear the country draft when the user starts a new quote. Do not put quote data in URLs, cookies, analytics, diagnostic logs, content requests, or server persistence. App-opened separate tabs should omit `opener` where relevant. A duplicated or opener-linked tab can inherit an initial copy and then diverge. The design promises no cross-tab or cross-device guarantees. [HTML Web Storage standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)

The US-01 step-2 handoff can be verified with a same-country route or narrow screen that allows going back. It owns no plan UI or plan business behavior. Future deep links to plans or summary check the matching country and current prerequisites, then navigate to the earliest incomplete step within that country. Client guards are wizard navigation controls. The data boundary is implemented by the public API shape and the absence of quote-write operations. [Angular Router guards](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/route-guards)

## Consequences for later stories

- **US-02** consumes a current, validated Step 1 snapshot and published active country plans. Store only one selected plan reference per quote along with the calculated price snapshot and its inputs or revision linkage as specified later. A change to inputs or available plans invalidates dependent selections or totals when the later rules require it. Recheck prerequisites before summary.
- **US-03** derives the review from current country fields and masks the identity document in presentation. Use stable field purpose metadata to locate the document independently of its label. Bind consent to the current terms revision and quote snapshot. Proposed duplicate protection is an atomic attempt transition in the same store, from eligible to processing before the asynchronous simulation starts. Only the matching attempt can settle, repeat clicks do not enqueue, success keeps one confirmation number for that completed quote, and a reported failure may retry. The US-03 spec and checkpoint will decide how reload handles a persisted processing attempt and completed receipt. No real gateway, card data or global idempotency service is implied.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Memory only | Lowest retention, with loss on reload and no reconciliation of previously saved data after refresh. |
| Browser persistent storage or IndexedDB | Longer recovery and broader synchronization options, with unnecessary fictitious customer-data retention and more cleanup or coordination. |
| Server quote collection or hosted state | Could support cross-device resume and global deduplication, contrary to the frontend-only customer and quote data boundary. |
| General-purpose state management library | Provides conventions for large applications. Three wizard steps can share a signal store without that dependency. |

Verify same-country Back and Forward, country-switch isolation, restoration plus reconciliation after reload, graceful storage failure, and exclusion of quote data from network requests. Exercise duplicate payment attempts and reload outcomes under US-03. US-01 traces to AC-US01-06, 08, 09, 13 and 14 and T-US01-07, 08, 09, 13 and 14.

[Angular Signals](https://angular.dev/guide/signals)

The goal is UI that looks like it was built by a design-aware engineer at a top company — not like it was generated by an AI. This means real design system adherence, proper accessibility, thoughtful interaction patterns, and no generic "AI aesthetic." ## When to Use - Building new UI components or pages - Modifying existing user-facing interfaces - Implementing responsive layouts - Adding interactivity or state management - Fixing visual or UX issues ## Verify With What the Project Has Run the project's own test, type-check, or lint commands. Don't install a framework, test runner, or type checker just to check your work; if the project has none, review the code against the [Verification](#verification) list and say what you could not run. ## Component Architecture ### File Structure Colocate everything related to a component: ``` src/components/ TaskList/ TaskList.tsx # Component implementation TaskList.test.tsx # Tests TaskList.stories.tsx # Storybook stories (if using) use-task-list.ts # Custom hook (if complex state) types.ts # Component-specific types (if needed) ``` ### Component Patterns **Prefer composition over configuration:** ```tsx // Good: Composable Tasks // Avoid: Over-configured } # Validate Input After Interaction ## The Problem Displaying validation errors the moment a user focuses on a field and starts typing is premature and distracting. DO start each message with an error icon that has a text alternative such as "Error" (the safest choice), or word every message as an error, for example "Please enter a valid email address.", and use the same approach for every error in the form. **Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-01-architecture-approval.md))  
**Applies to** US-01, with shared boundaries for US-02 and US-03  
**Basis** [US-01 Draft 3](../../spec/US-01.md), [specification approval](../approvals/US-01-spec-approval.md), assessment pp. 1–3 and 6–9

## Context

One Angular build serves Colombia and Chile. Editors publish independent country configuration in Strapi. The URL identifies the active country, including on reload and browser Back or Forward. The frontend needs published content and all customer and quote data stays in the browser.

## Proposed decision

- Use one client-rendered Angular application and one standalone Router tree. Serve the country selector at `/` and recognize `/:country/quote/details` for US-01. Reserve `plans` and `summary` children for the later steps. An explicit in-country entry route may link to Details. Unsupported country segments show the recoverable country-selection screen and retain the attempted URL. Accept exact uppercase `CO` and `CL` and replace the history entry with the lowercase canonical path for the same country. Other case variants remain unsupported. SPA navigation fallback applies to app paths, with API paths and asset requests kept separate.
- Decode the current Router parameter to `co | cl` before accessing content or quote state. React to parameter changes even when the Router reuses the component. Same-country wizard navigation can reuse its last valid, in-memory configuration. Initial load, page reload, country transition (including return to a previously visited country), and explicit retry require a new request. Clear ready status at refresh start. Cancel superseded reads and check both country and request generation before committing a response. A late or failed response leaves quote data intact and never renders as current. The URL carries the country and step only.
- Use a Strapi country enum, Draft & Publish, and one **Form Configuration collection document per country**, containing the complete field list as repeatable components. Each field inherits country from its owning form. This makes punctuation, copy, additions and removals, ordering, and option or validation edits one publishable snapshot. Editors use Content Manager for entries and may stage drafts without changing the live form. The serving controller reads published documents explicitly and treats multiple published form documents for one country as invalid rather than picking a winner. Seed by country without clobbering subsequent editorial changes. A stable editorial field key is distinct from Strapi's internal component IDs. [Strapi Document Service publication status](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/status)
- US-02 can use a separate Plan collection filtered by requested country, published status, and active flag, with stable plan identifiers, ordered plans, stored price/currency, coverages, benefits, and a recommended flag. US-03 can use a separate country Terms document with published text and a revision identifier. Their precise shapes, prices, and publication/acceptance rules belong to their future specifications. Changes to plans or terms need only their own publication.

## Public read boundary

The browser uses a same-origin `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/form` routed to Strapi through the static app host. Keep Strapi's ordinary Content API authorization enabled and grant the Public role the single custom `api::quote-content.quote-content.readForm` action. Enable neither generated CRUD routes for these content types nor public draft, preview, plugin, search, media, or admin actions. The frontend sends no authorization token. The static host proxies the dedicated read path only and returns no substitute SPA HTML for unmatched API paths. Admin access is a separate local binding and uses Strapi admin authentication for editorial access. [Strapi routing](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/backend-customization/routes), [Users & Permissions](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/features/users-permissions)

The controller takes the canonical country path parameter and no caller-controlled filters, locale, population, or publication selectors. It explicitly queries published data, populates only the known components, validates the whole content projection, and maps an allowlisted DTO. Success is `200` with `{ schemaVersion: 1, country, fields }` (see [ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md)). Public outcomes are `400 INVALID_REQUEST` for unsupported query inputs, `404 UNSUPPORTED_COUNTRY` for an unsupported API path code, `404 FORM_NOT_PUBLISHED` for no published document, `503 FORM_UNAVAILABLE` for configuration invalidity or duplicate documents, and `503 CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE` for CMS retrieval failure. A published document with no fields is invalid. Use a stable `{ error: { code } }` response without stack traces, internal IDs, or raw data. Use `Cache-Control: no-store` on these responses and bypass intermediary cache for this API path. The frontend still decodes success bodies and rejects country or version mismatches. Errors use local accessible fallback copy and retry. Future plan and terms routes require separate public actions after those stories' approvals.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| URL query, cookies, or geolocation | A query is shareable but easier to drop between steps. Device-derived defaults conflict with explicit URL country selection. |
| One frontend per market or per-locale builds | Independent releases could isolate releases, at the cost of duplicate deployment and violating the single-build requirement. |
| Strapi i18n as the country axis | Convenient for translations of shared records. Country controls eligibility, currency, and fields as well as language, so a country enum models the business boundary directly. |
| One Strapi record per field with public collection reads | Easier independent field editing, with more fragmented publication, larger permission surface, and more coupling to Strapi's REST shape. |
| An authenticated BFF with a server-side Strapi token | Supports private content at the cost of additional runtime and secret management. The proposed custom Strapi route already serves a narrow public projection. |

The custom route and decoder are deliberate maintenance costs. Editors can publish changes within the supported versioned vocabulary. New field primitives and incompatible contract changes are engineering changes. Confirm exact Public action registration and route permissions in the pinned Strapi version during implementation before exposing the route. Verify both canonical URLs after a hard reload, draft exclusion, rejection of cross-country responses and query overrides, denial of anonymous writes and generated reads, and published change pickup without rebuilding Angular. # ADR-002 — Typed dynamic form contract and reconciliation

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-01-architecture-approval.md))  
**Applies to** US-01, with stable fields and roles for US-02 and US-03  
**Basis** [US-01 Draft 3](../../spec/US-01.md), especially AC-US01-02–04, 07–10 and 12–16, and [ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md)

## Context

Strapi editors need to change field content and validation without rebuilding Angular. The application must reject a bad configuration atomically, preserve a compatible draft across changes, and display one configured error per field. A dynamic CMS key cannot provide static knowledge of its eventual widget or value type.

## Proposed decision

### Contract and failure behavior

Decode `unknown` once at each trust boundary using framework-independent TypeScript guards that produce a discriminated `FieldDefinition` union. A small shared workspace contract can supply the decoder, pure validation and fixtures to Strapi's projection and Angular's consumer. It carries no Angular or Strapi dependency and no customer data. Keep Strapi's nested editor representation behind its explicit projection. Contract version 1 is a fixed envelope with an exact version, the requested canonical country, and a nonempty fields array. Render content strings as text, including labels, help and errors. Each field has the following projected properties.

| Property | Version 1 proposal |
| --- | --- |
| `id`, `label`, `helpText`, `errorMessage` | Stable editor-maintained ID unique within the country form, Spanish label and fallback field error, and a required help-text property that permits an empty string. IDs are restricted opaque strings, protected from reserved object keys and independent of labels, order, and Strapi component IDs. |
| `kind`, `required`, `order` | One supported kind, a Boolean required flag, and a nonnegative safe-integer order. Sort by order, then by ID on a tie. Country is inherited from the form. |
| `rules` | Ordered array, possibly empty. Each rule specifies a recognized operator, its typed arguments when relevant, and its configured Spanish message. Order is the editor's array order. |
| `options`, `defaultValue` | Options are permitted only on selects and require stable unique option IDs and nonempty labels within each select. An omitted default means unset. A present default must meet the field's representation, available options, and configured rules. Fresh required selects start unset, so publishing a default for one is invalid. |
| `purpose` | Optional semantic marker, unique per reserved role. A usable form contains one required `dateOfBirth` date with `minimumAge` 18 and one required `vehicleYear` number with `vehicleYearRange`. `identityDocument` and `licensePlate` markers, when present, use text fields. This enables masking and pricing without relying on visible labels. |

Reject missing mandatory properties, missing published fields, date or number representation errors in rule arguments, incompatible defaults, unknown types or operators, duplicate IDs, and required selects with no valid options. Validate each option. An invalid option definition fails the snapshot. Allow an optional select to have no options and remain unset. Reject inverted range endpoints and a duplicate required rule. A rejected refresh never partially updates the view or the stored draft. Apply the error and retry behavior in ADR-001. Enforce size limits on fields, options, and text at the contract boundary. Choose exact limits during implementation against fixtures and document them.

### Type and rule compatibility

| Kinds and values | Supported operators |
| --- | --- |
| Text, a string, including document numbers and plates | `required`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `email` |
| Number, a finite JavaScript number | `required`, `min`, `max`, `vehicleYearRange` for the vehicle-year purpose |
| Select, a listed stable option ID string | `required` |
| Date, a valid Gregorian ISO calendar-date string `YYYY-MM-DD` | `required`, `minDate`, `maxDate`, `minimumAge` for the date-of-birth purpose |
| Checkbox, a Boolean | `required`, which requires explicit `true` for a required checkbox |

- Keep a single required check. The field flag controls requiredness. An optional explicit `required` rule is valid only when the flag is true and supplies the required message. A required flag without the rule uses the field's configured error message. Required checks distinguish missing values from numeric zero. Whitespace-only text is empty for the required check and stored document or plate strings retain leading zeros. Non-required rules treat an unset value as inapplicable. An invalid typed entry is distinct from an unset value. Apply validators to every field and retain the ordered outcomes. The required error wins when present, then the first failing configured rule, then the field fallback for an invalid representation no configured rule describes.
- Length and age arguments are nonnegative integers, and lengths count Unicode code points. Numeric bounds are finite and inclusive. Vehicle year requires a safe integer and uses local browser Gregorian year Y with inclusive Y−20 through Y+1. Date bounds are valid ISO dates and inclusive. Calculate age using Gregorian calendar components and the browser's local civil date via an injectable clock, avoiding UTC parsing shifts. Propose March 1 for a February 29 birthday in non-leap years in the simulator. `required`, `email`, and `vehicleYearRange` take no argument.
- Treat patterns as declarative whole-value checks in a bounded safe subset. Propose bounded character classes, literal segments, and bounded repetitions, with no backreferences, lookaround, groups, or unbounded repetition. Cap both pattern and input lengths. Use a bounded non-backtracking matcher for the subset or equivalent implementation whose cost is bounded on rejected input. Validate editor patterns before the config reaches ready state. This makes formatting changes publishable while keeping pattern matching predictable.

### Angular form and accessibility

Use Typed Reactive Forms with `FormRecord<FormControl<FieldValue | null>>` and a discriminated field/view model. Keys are dynamic and the control's static value type is the common union. Narrow by the decoded field kind and normalize at the control adapter and output boundaries. Use actual typed number and Boolean values, preserve meaningful empty or unset state, and track rendered elements by stable ID. Stay with native inputs and selects and an unset, non-selectable required-select placeholder. The first invalid field gets focus on an unsuccessful Continue. Keep Continue available after the configuration is ready, with application validation controlling progress and custom messages. Use native form semantics with an explicit Angular submit handler and no browser validation bubbles masking configured messages. On blur expose that field's message, on change reevaluate touched fields, and on submit expose all applicable errors. Associate visible errors and help through stable DOM IDs and `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid` when showing an error. Use concise status announcements for loading and retry, and avoid announcing the same validation error twice when moving focus. [Angular typed forms](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/typed-forms)

### Deterministic reconciliation

Rebuild the draft from the latest valid fields by ID instead of mutating the old key map in place. Omit removed or replaced IDs and obsolete select options entirely. For new IDs apply a valid allowed default or leave unset. For existing IDs preserve representable values and keep label, help, and order edits independent, even if updated business rules make a preserved value invalid. This lets users correct a value after a stricter constraint is published. Check the previous kind as well as the primitive value. Preserve a date as text, or text as a date only when it is already a valid ISO date. Clear other kind changes without implicit coercion. Select values require membership in the new option IDs and never migrate by label. Revalidate every field against the current clock and refreshed rules, write the clean snapshot atomically, and gate progression on the result. A restored valid required select stays selected. A fresh one, or one with an obsolete selection, shows its placeholder.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Hardcoded Angular fields or a FormGroup with fixed keys | Strong static key typing, with a code change for each CMS field change. |
| Untyped forms or a general JSON Schema rendering engine | Simpler generalization, with weaker app-level typing or an extra dependency and a harder-to-explain CMS contract. |
| Signal Forms | Fits a signal-first model and is stable in Angular 22. The proposed Angular 21 baseline and requested form preference favor Typed Reactive Forms. Signals still own non-control state. |
| Directly execute CMS regexes or arbitrary editor rules | Broader flexibility, with less predictable runtime cost and harder validation of whole snapshots. |

The proposal makes unsupported widgets and rule language changes schema work. It protects the required age and year invariants while permitting published changes to supported field content. The type matrix, safe pattern subset, date boundary convention, and required-select default restriction are proposed architecture decisions. Verify DTO acceptance and rejection in both consumers, age and year boundaries, required-first and rule order, data reconciliation, stale response rejection, keyboard focus, and the two required-select states. See T-US01-02–06, 08–10, 12 and 14–16. The final quote-summary view remains under US-03.

# Frontend UI Engineering

## Overview

Build production-quality user interfaces that are accessible, performant, and visually polished. The goal is UI that looks like it was built by a design-aware engineer at a top company — not like it was generated by an AI. This means real design system adherence, proper accessibility, thoughtful interaction patterns, and no generic "AI aesthetic."

## When to Use

- Building new UI components or pages
- Modifying existing user-facing interfaces
- Implementing responsive layouts
- Adding interactivity or state management
- Fixing visual or UX issues

## Verify With What the Project Has

Run the project's own test, type-check, or lint commands. Don't install a framework, test runner, or type checker just to check your work; if the project has none, review the code against the [Verification](#verification) list and say what you could not run.

## Component Architecture

Colocate everything related to a component:

```
src/components/
  TaskList/
    TaskList.tsx          # Component implementation
    TaskList.test.tsx     # Tests
    TaskList.stories.tsx  # Storybook stories (if using)
    use-task-list.ts      # Custom hook (if complex state)
    types.ts              # Component-specific types (if needed)
```

### Component Patterns

**Prefer composition over configuration:**

```tsx

  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Tasks</CardTitle>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardBody>

The `:user-invalid` pseudo-class solves this perfectly. For a required field, it will not match on page load. It will only match if:
1.  The user interacts with the field (e.g., types a character and deletes it) and then leaves it (blur), leaving it empty.
2.  The user attempts to submit the form while the field is empty.

### Implementation Strategy

1.  **HTML Constraint**: Add the `required` attribute to your inputs.
2.  **Visual Feedback**: Use `:user-invalid` to style the border red and show a "Required" helper text.
3.  **Timing**: Rely on the browser's native timing for visual feedback. You don't need `onBlur` handlers to add a `touched` class anymore, though some JavaScript is still needed to sync ARIA attributes (see below).
4.  **Error Text**: Show visible error text with the error styling, so the error isn't shown by color alone. Start each message with an error icon that has a text alternative such as "Error" (the safest choice), or word every message as an error, for example "Name is required.", and use the same approach for every error in the form.
5.  **Error Link**: List the error message in the field's `aria-describedby` only while the field is invalid, so screen readers read it with the field. A reference in the markup would read the hidden message from page load. The script in section 3 does this for each field whose `data-error` attribute is set to its error message's `id`.

## Implementation Guide

### 1. HTML Structure
```html
<form id="feedback-form">
  <div class="field">
    <label for="full-name">Full Name</label>
    <!-- Set data-error to the error message's id. The aria-invalid script lists that id in aria-describedby while the field is invalid. -->
    <input
      type="text"
      id="full-name"
      name="full-name"
      required
      data-error="name-error"
    >
    <!-- MANDATORY: Include an icon or distinct non-color indicator alongside error text -->
    <div id="name-error" class="error-msg">
      <span role="img" aria-label="Error">❌</span> This field is required.
    </div>
  </div>
</form>
```

### 2. CSS
```css
.error-msg {
  display: none;
  color: #d93025;
  font-size: 0.875rem;
  margin-top: 0.25rem;
}

/*
  Only highlight empty required fields AFTER the user interacts with them or attempts submission.
  MANDATORY: Provide multiple indicators (border shift + helper text/icon) to avoid color-only state communication.
*/
input:user-invalid {
  border-color: #d93025;
  background-color: #fce8e6;
}

input:user-invalid + .error-msg {
  display: block;
}

/* Optional: Subtle indicator for required fields that are valid */
input:required:user-valid {
  border-color: #188038;
  border-width: 2px;
}
```

### 3. JavaScript State Synchronization

MANDATORY: Because `:user-invalid` is a visual state, you MUST provide a JavaScript bridge to sync `aria-invalid="true"` dynamically for assistive technologies when a user blurs an invalid field or attempts submission, deriving it from `:user-invalid`, not `checkValidity()`, which is already false when a user tabs through an untouched field.

Native `:user-invalid` does not automatically sync with ARIA attributes. Add the following JavaScript to keep `aria-invalid` in sync with the visual state:

* Set `aria-invalid="false"` until `:user-invalid` matches, rather than leaving it unset. Firefox and Safari expose an empty `required` field as invalid from page load, and Chromium doesn't expose an empty `required` field as invalid after interaction unless `aria-invalid="true"` is set.
* Link each field to its error message by setting the field's `data-error` attribute to the error message's `id` (`data-error="email-error"` for `<div id="email-error">`), and let the script list that `id` in `aria-describedby` only while the field is invalid. Don't reference the error from `aria-describedby` in the markup: the error element is always in the page, and text that `aria-describedby` references is announced even when it's hidden.
* Announce an error that appears when the user leaves or changes a field through one polite live region for the page, a moment later so it doesn't talk over the next field. Don't make each error message a live region: a live region that is shown, rather than changed, isn't announced reliably. After a failed submit, move focus to the first invalid field so that its error is announced instead.

```javascript
// List the field's error message (the id in data-error) in aria-describedby only while
// it's shown: text that aria-describedby references is announced even when it's hidden.
const linkError = (el, shown) => {
  const errorId = el.dataset.error;
  if (!errorId) return;
  const ids = (el.getAttribute('aria-describedby') || '').split(/\s+/).filter((id) => id && id !== errorId);
  if (shown) ids.push(errorId);
  if (ids.length) el.setAttribute('aria-describedby', ids.join(' '));
  else el.removeAttribute('aria-describedby');
};

// One polite live region for the page announces an error that appears when the user
// leaves or changes a field. Run this once the form is in the page.
const announcer = document.createElement('div');
announcer.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');
announcer.classList.add('visually-hidden');
document.body.append(announcer);
let announceTimer;
let announcedField;

// Text as a screen reader reads it: icons' text alternatives in, aria-hidden text out.
const spokenText = (node) => {
  const copy = node.cloneNode(true);
  copy.querySelectorAll('[aria-hidden="true"]').forEach((n) => n.remove());
  copy.querySelectorAll('[role="img"][aria-label]').forEach((n) => n.replaceWith(`${n.getAttribute('aria-label')}: `));
  return copy.textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
};
const announceError = (el) => {
  const error = document.getElementById(el.dataset.error);
  if (!error) return;
  const label = el.labels?.[0] ? `${spokenText(el.labels[0])}: ` : '';
  clearTimeout(announceTimer);
  announcer.textContent = '';
  announcedField = el;
  // Wait until the screen reader has announced the field that receives focus next.
  announceTimer = setTimeout(() => { announcer.textContent = label + spokenText(error); }, 500);
};

// Sync aria-invalid with the CSS :user-invalid state. Only form fields are synced, and
// an aria-invalid="true" that this script didn't set (for example from a server check)
// is left alone.
const flagged = new WeakSet();
// Fields whose current error has been announced, or read out by focus after a failed
// submit. A field can become invalid while the user types, so this is tracked separately.
const announced = new WeakSet();
const syncAria = (el, announce = false) => {
  if (!el.matches?.('input, select, textarea')) return;
  const invalid = el.matches(':user-invalid');
  if (invalid) {
    if (announce && !announced.has(el)) {
      announceError(el);
      announced.add(el);
    }
    el.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    linkError(el, true);
    flagged.add(el);
  } else if (flagged.has(el) || el.getAttribute('aria-invalid') !== 'true') {
    el.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'false');
    linkError(el, false);
    flagged.delete(el);
    announced.delete(el);
    // Clear a fixed field's announcement so it isn't found later when reading the page.
    if (announcedField === el) {
      clearTimeout(announceTimer);
      announcer.textContent = '';
    }
  }
};

// Start every field at aria-invalid="false".
document.querySelectorAll('input, select, textarea').forEach((el) => syncAria(el));

// Update on blur (to show and announce an error) and input (to clear it)
document.addEventListener('blur', (e) => syncAria(e.target, true), true);
document.addEventListener('input', (e) => {
  if (e.target.hasAttribute('aria-invalid')) syncAria(e.target);
});

// Checkboxes, radio buttons and other controls that commit on 'change' can become
// :user-invalid without losing focus, so update on change too.
document.addEventListener('change', (e) => syncAria(e.target, true), true);

// A failed submit fires 'invalid' on each failing field, including required fields the
// user never touched, so update those too. 'invalid' doesn't bubble. Focus moving to the
// first invalid field announces its error, so these aren't announced.
document.addEventListener('invalid', (e) => {
  announced.add(e.target);
  syncAria(e.target);
}, true);

// Reset clears :user-invalid after the 'reset' event, so update each field afterwards.
document.addEventListener('reset', (e) => {
  setTimeout(() => [...e.target.elements].forEach((el) => syncAria(el)));
}, true);
```

Hide the live region with the `.visually-hidden` utility:

```css
/* Hides content visually but keeps it in the accessibility tree */
.visually-hidden:where(:not(:focus-within, :active)) {
  position: absolute !important;
  clip-path: inset(50%) !important;
  overflow: hidden !important;
  width: 1px !important;
  height: 1px !important;
  margin: -1px !important;
  padding: 0 !important;
  border: 0 !important;
  white-space: nowrap !important;
}
```

## Fallbacking & Browser Support

### Fallbacks & browser support for :user-valid and :user-invalid

Baseline status for :user-valid and :user-invalid: Widely available. It's been Baseline since 2023-11-02.
Supported by: Chrome 119 (Oct 2023), Edge 119 (Nov 2023), Firefox 88 (Apr 2021), and Safari 16.5 (May 2023).

### CSS for Fallback

```css
/* Applies to every field that can be invalid (input, select, textarea). :is() keeps the
   rule working where :user-invalid isn't supported: in a plain selector list, one
   unsupported selector drops the whole rule. */
:is(:user-invalid, .user-invalid-fallback) {
  border-color: #d93025;
  background-color: #fce8e6;
}

:is(:user-invalid, .user-invalid-fallback) + .error-msg {
  display: block;
}
```

### JavaScript Fallback

Use a reusable utility that tracks interaction state using a `WeakMap`. This avoids polluting the DOM with "dirty" classes or data attributes.

```javascript
const UserInvalidFallback = (() => {
  const dirtyState = new WeakMap();

  const updateState = (input) => {
    // validity.valid gives the current state without firing an 'invalid' event, as checkValidity() does.
    const isValid = input.validity.valid;

    // Update both visual and ARIA state
    input.classList.toggle('user-invalid-fallback', !isValid);
    input.classList.toggle('user-valid-fallback', isValid);

    input.setAttribute('aria-invalid', isValid ? 'false' : 'true');
    linkError(input, !isValid);
  };

  // List the error message (the id in data-error) in aria-describedby only while it's
  // shown: text that aria-describedby references is announced even when it's hidden.
  const linkError = (input, shown) => {
    const errorId = input.dataset.error;
    if (!errorId) return;
    const ids = (input.getAttribute('aria-describedby') || '').split(/\s+/).filter((id) => id && id !== errorId);
    if (shown) ids.push(errorId);
    if (ids.length) input.setAttribute('aria-describedby', ids.join(' '));
    else input.removeAttribute('aria-describedby');
  };

  const handleEvent = (event) => {
    const input = event.target;

    if (event.type === 'reset') {
      const controls = input.elements || [];
      for (const control of controls) {
        dirtyState.delete(control);
        control.classList.remove('user-invalid-fallback');
        control.classList.remove('user-valid-fallback');
        if (control.matches('input, select, textarea')) control.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'false');
        if (control.dataset?.error) linkError(control, false);
      }
      return;
    }

    if (!input.checkValidity) return;

    // A submit attempt counts as interaction: the browser fires 'invalid' on each failing
    // field, including required fields the user never touched, so flag them all.
    if (event.type === 'invalid') {
      dirtyState.set(input, { hasInteracted: true, hasBlurred: true });
      updateState(input);
      return;
    }

    if (event.type === 'input' || event.type === 'change') {
      const state = dirtyState.get(input) || { hasInteracted: false, hasBlurred: false };
      state.hasInteracted = true;
      dirtyState.set(input, state);
      if (state.hasBlurred) {
        updateState(input);
      }
    } else if (event.type === 'blur') {
      const state = dirtyState.get(input) || { hasInteracted: false, hasBlurred: false };
      state.hasBlurred = true;
      dirtyState.set(input, state);
      if (state.hasInteracted) {
        updateState(input);
      }
    }
  };

  const init = (root = document) => {
    if (CSS.supports('selector(:user-invalid)')) return;

    // Firefox and Safari expose an empty required field as invalid from page load.
    root.querySelectorAll('input, select, textarea').forEach((el) => {
      if (!el.hasAttribute('aria-invalid')) el.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'false');
    });

    root.addEventListener('blur', handleEvent, true); // Capture phase
    root.addEventListener('input', handleEvent);
    root.addEventListener('change', handleEvent);
    root.addEventListener('invalid', handleEvent, true); // invalid doesn't bubble
    root.addEventListener('reset', handleEvent, true); // Capture resets
  };

  return { init };
})();

// Initialize for a specific form
const form = document.querySelector('#demo-form');
UserInvalidFallback.init(form);
```

## Other Considerations

1.  **Asterisks**: It is still best practice to indicate required fields visually (e.g., with an asterisk `*`) in the label, so users know what to expect *before* they interact. Explain the asterisk once before the form (for example, "Fields marked * are required."), and wrap it in `<span aria-hidden="true">*</span>`, because the `required` attribute already makes screen readers announce "required".
2.  **Submit Buttons**: Unlike `disabled` buttons, keep your submit button enabled. If the user clicks it, the browser will automatically trigger `:user-invalid` on all empty required fields and focus the first one. This is excellent for accessibility and UX.

# Angular New App

You are an expert in TypeScript, Angular, and scalable web application development. You write functional, maintainable, performant, and accessible code following Angular and TypeScript best practices. You have access to tools to create new Angular apps.

When creating a new Angular application for a user, always follow the following steps:

1. **Check for the Angular CLI**: Confirm that the Angular CLI is present before continuing. Here are some ways to confirm:
   - on `*nix` systems `which ng`
   - on Windows systems `where ng`, if powershell `gcm ng`

   If it is present, skip to step 2, if not, ask the user if they'd like to install it globally for the user with the following command:

   `npm install -g @angular/cli`

   _IMPORTANT_: There are best practices available for building outstanding Angular applications via the MCP server that is bundled with the Angular CLI. Available through `ng mcp` and the `get_best_practices`.

2. **Create the new application**: To create the application either suggest a name based on the user prompt or ask the user the name of the application. Create the application with the following command:

   `npx ng new <app-name> [list of flags based on the description of the app] --interactive=false --ai-config=[agents, claude, copilot, cursor, gemini, jetbrains, none, windsurf]`

   _Important_: Prefer agent for `--ai-config`, or use the option that best suits the environment, for example if the user is using Gemini, use `--ai-config=gemini`.

   Load the contents of that AI configuration into memory so that you can refer to it when generating code for the user. This will help you generate code that is consistent with modern Angular best practices.

   Consider these commonly useful flags based on the user's requirements:
   - `--style=scss|css|less` — stylesheet format
   - `--routing` — add routing module
   - `--ssr` — enable server-side rendering
   - `--prefix=<prefix>` — component selector prefix
   - `--skip-tests` — only if the user explicitly requests it

3. Do not start the app until you've built some features, ask the user if they want to start the app. You can always run `npx ng build` to check for errors and repair them.

4. Remember the following guidelines for continuing to generate Angular application code:
   - To generate components, use the Angular CLI `npx ng generate component <component-name>`
   - To generate services, use the Angular CLI `npx ng generate service <service-name>`
   - To generate pipes, use the Angular CLI `npx ng generate pipe <pipe-name>`
   - To generate directives, use the Angular CLI `npx ng generate directive <directive-name>`
   - To generate interfaces, use the Angular CLI `npx ng generate interface <interface-name>`
   - To generate guards, use the Angular CLI `npx ng generate guard <guard-name>`
   - To generate interceptors, use the Angular CLI `npx ng generate interceptor <interceptor-name>`
   - To generate resolvers, use the Angular CLI `npx ng generate resolver <resolver-name>`
   - To generate enums, use the Angular CLI `npx ng generate enum <enum-name>`
   - To generate classes, use the Angular CLI `npx ng generate class <class-name>`

   _IMPORTANT_: Take note of the path returned from running the generate commands so that you know exactly where the new files are.

   Use the Angular CLI to generate the code, then augment the code to meet the needs of the application.

5. To add tailwind, run `npx ng add tailwindcss`. After that, you do not have to do anything else, you can start using tailwind classes in your Angular application. Follow the best practices for tailwind v4 here, learn more if needed: https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide.

_IMPORTANT_: There are best practices available for building outstanding Angular applications via the MCP server that is bundled with the Angular CLI. Available through `npx ng mcp` and the `get_best_practices`.
# US-01 — Technology stack proposal

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-01-architecture-approval.md))  
**Scope** US-01 architecture and the shared foundations for US-02 and US-03  
**Basis** [US-01 Draft 3](../../spec/US-01.md) and the technical assessment, pp. 1–3 and 6–9

## Recommendation and compatibility

Recommend the proposed stack with Angular **21.x LTS**, Strapi **5.x**, and a common patched **Node.js 24 LTS** line. Angular 21 allows Node 24 and TypeScript 5.9.x. Strapi 5 documents support for Node 24 and SQLite 3, and Playwright and pnpm 11 support the same Node line. Pin current compatible patches and the Node container version when scaffolding. Angular workspace packages, the Angular CLI, and Angular ESLint use the same major. Strapi can retain its own tested TypeScript toolchain, with the shared contract kept compatible with both consumers. Angular 22 is an upgrade option with a longer support horizon and TypeScript 6 requirements. Angular 21 LTS provides the requested capabilities with a smaller compatibility surface for this assessment. Review an upgrade before its LTS ends if the app continues beyond the assessment. [Angular compatibility](https://angular.dev/reference/versions), [Angular release support](https://angular.dev/reference/releases), [Strapi prerequisites](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/quick-start), [Node release lines](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases), [Playwright installation](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro), [pnpm 11 release notes](https://pnpm.io/blog/releases/11.0)

| Preference | Proposal, alternative, and trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Angular 21+ | Angular CLI application build, standalone components, built-in control flow, and strict TypeScript. Serve client-rendered assets from one static host. SSR or a separate build per market adds hosting/build complexity to a runtime-configured wizard. |
| Strapi 5+ | Use Content Manager, Draft & Publish, and scoped public reads. Direct generated collection reads are quicker to set up but expose a wider query and contract surface. Follow [ADR-001](../adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md). |
| Tailwind CSS 4 | Use the Angular-supported PostCSS path with Tailwind's v4 plugin and CSS import, and use CSS theme tokens for shared design. Keep utility names statically discoverable and render CMS copy as text. Plain component CSS would remove tooling at the cost of more repetitive layout rules. Support the intersection of Angular 21's 2025-10-20 Baseline browser set and Tailwind v4's documented CSS requirements, including Chrome 111+, Firefox 128+, and Safari 16.4+. Current Playwright engines provide cross-browser smoke without certifying every minimum version. [Angular Tailwind setup](https://angular.dev/guide/tailwind), [Tailwind browser support](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/compatibility), [Angular browser support](https://angular.dev/reference/versions#browser-support) |
| Vitest and Angular TestBed | Use the Angular CLI unit test builder and its Vitest baseline. Run pure domain tests directly in Vitest and use TestBed for components, routing, and HTTP doubles. Browser-only interaction, layout, and keyboard checks use Playwright. Karma adds another browser-runner setup with overlap for this project. [Angular v21 release announcement](https://blog.angular.dev/announcing-angular-v21-57946c34f14b), [Angular unit testing](https://angular.dev/guide/testing) |
| Playwright | Separate browser test suite targeting the served app and disposable seeded Strapi. Start with Chromium and run WebKit and Firefox smoke for shared keyboard and rendering behavior. The package adds browser binaries and CI cost. Component tests alone cannot verify routing, publishing, and runtime integration. [Playwright browsers](https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers) |
| Typed Reactive Forms | Use dynamic keyed controls with a shared value type and a runtime-decoded discriminated field contract. Angular cannot infer exact static control types at CMS-defined keys. Template-driven or untyped forms would weaken the boundary. Signal Forms can be reconsidered with an Angular upgrade. [ADR-002](../adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md), [Angular typed forms](https://angular.dev/guide/forms/typed-forms) |
| Angular Signals | Keep quote and view state in a small Signals store. Reactive Forms still own control lifecycle. RxJS can handle cancelable request sequencing, with no extra state library. A general-purpose store would add new dependencies and patterns for a three-step wizard. [ADR-003](../adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md), [Angular Signals](https://angular.dev/guide/signals) |
| Angular Router | Use one standalone route tree keyed by ISO country path code. The URL remains shareable and reloadable. A cookie, query, or language-based routing would offer weaker country-state boundaries. [ADR-001](../adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) |
| Tabler Icons | Copy individual reviewed SVG files from the official project, retain the upstream license notice with the distributed assets, and use accessible names on controls and labels where needed. Use local SVGs and treat decorative icons as hidden from assistive technology. An icon library adds a dependency and a CDN adds a runtime request. [Official icon catalog](https://tabler.io/icons), [Tabler Icons MIT license](https://tabler.io/license) |
| Angular ESLint and Prettier | Use Angular ESLint matching Angular CLI 21 with compatible ESLint flat configuration and template checks. Use a separately invoked, exact-pinned Prettier for formatting, leaving lint rules to address code. A general ESLint setup alone misses Angular template checks. [Angular ESLint compatibility](https://github.com/angular-eslint/angular-eslint#supported-angular-cli-versions), [Prettier installation](https://prettier.io/docs/install) |
| pnpm | Use one pnpm 11 workspace with one lockfile, an exact `packageManager` pin, frozen installs in container and automation, and a narrowly reviewed `allowBuilds` configuration for needed native scripts. npm is a viable fallback but would create a second install convention. Recheck Strapi native packages and Angular builder dependencies with the pinned pnpm version. [pnpm workspaces](https://pnpm.io/workspaces), [pnpm 11 release notes](https://pnpm.io/blog/releases/11.0) |
| Docker Compose | Use a Node 24 build/runtime family and a small static host container serving Angular and proxying its same-origin content readers. A host install or independent services would spread prerequisites and startup steps. [Compose startup ordering](https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/startup-order/) |
| SQLite for Strapi internal persistence | One Strapi instance, one named volume for CMS content and administrative metadata, and no additional database service. Use a glibc-based Node image and verify its native SQLite binding on each supported container architecture. SQLite has a simpler startup and backup model for the assessment. It carries single-instance and write-concurrency limits, which are acceptable here. PostgreSQL offers a path for a different workload and is outside the proposed scope. [Strapi database configuration](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/configurations/database) |
| Frontend-only customer and quote state | Keep policyholder and vehicle data, quote state, plan selection, and simulated payment state in the frontend. Strapi content and read logs contain no request body or query with that data. Use tab-scoped retention for fictitious data only and document storage-loss behavior. [ADR-003](../adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) |

These are documentation-backed compatibility selections. Their exact package and container builds have not been exercised.

## Proposed startup and verification

- Organize the workspace under `frontend/` and `backend/`, with a smallest-necessary TypeScript workspace contract shared by both and an isolated Playwright suite. Use one browser origin. Strapi remains a private Compose service for app traffic, with a separate loopback admin binding for local editorial review. Static hosting serves Angular's deep-link fallback and proxies only the dedicated content reader URLs. Generate or inject Strapi-only startup secrets locally without putting them in the repository or browser. Admin provisioning is separate from the public app's readiness.
- Target `docker compose up --build` on a clean checkout. Use a one-time, idempotent seed step for published CO and CL forms and the minimum custom Public permission. Seed through server-side Strapi facilities. Verify readiness from this initialization and HTTP listener health while preserving usability if an editor unpublishes a country form later. Record initialization completion in the CMS volume so restart preserves editorial changes and deliberately removed entries. Use fictitious fixtures and avoid a pre-seeded admin password. US-02 and US-03 extend the seed with plan and term content in their own approved increments.
- In US-01 verification, cover decoder, validation, and reconciliation units, integrated route races, behavior through the same-origin proxy, and a real Strapi publication change consumed after reload without rebuilding Angular. Verify public access to the one intended reader, anonymous denial of other endpoints, draft exclusion, duplicate/empty/malformed configuration recovery, country isolation, keyboard and mobile/desktop usability, and clean-tree startup plus restart with preserved edits. Check native SQLite loaded in the runtime container and exact resolved package compatibility before treating the stack as verified.
- Full-flow Playwright coverage waits until US-02 and US-03 are implemented under their own checkpoints. Verify a complete simulated quote for at least one country and smoke the other, using both countries' seed data. Later verification covers country currency, active/published plans, plan selection, terms revision, masked summary, payment failure and retry, and duplicate protection. The US-01 step-transition test does not require an implemented plans UI.

## Review choices

Approve the stack and [country/content](../adr/ADR-001-multi-country-content.md), [dynamic form](../adr/ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md), and [wizard state](../adr/ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) proposals together or request changes to individual items. The defaults proposed for human review are exact uppercase country normalization, session storage for same-tab reload retention, an allowed bounded pattern subset, March 1 treatment of leap-day birthdays in non-leap years, and the restriction on defaults for required selects. If older browser versions must be supported beyond the stated intersection, provide the target versions before implementation. Pricing inputs, final plan and terms contracts, and simulated payment reload/receipt policy are decisions for the applicable later stories.
